about: Harder end-to-end evaluation questions (ids 101+): plain-language, Hinglish, two-Act, BNS-versus-IPC, 'not found', and (129-134) consumer, property, constitutional, defamation, workplace and a short query. DRAFT: the expected sections were written by Claude and are NOT yet checked by a lawyer. Each gold has `act` (title prefix in Neon), `section` (for humans), `anchor` (text that must appear in the section body, used to find it in Neon) and optional `alts` (other accepted sections for the same expectation: any one counts). `expect: notfound` = the right answer is that the sources do not contain it. `oldLaw` = the repealed section the answer should mention as 'previously ...' (rule: answer from the current law, name the old one). `mustMention` = regexes the answer must all match. `forbid` = [{act, numbers}] sections that must NOT be cited (not applicable to the situation). `skip` = question kept for the lawyer but not scored because the data is missing. `review` = note for the lawyer. General checks on every question: an answer that opens with 'I couldn't find...' while the expected section was shown scores no 'judged right' point.

questions.question: My tenant isn't paying rent, what can I do?

golds.anchor: by forfeiture

questions.review: Accept TPA s.106 or s.111 (s.106 is garbled in our data, so only s.111 can be matched). A good answer must say that eviction for non-payment of rent is mainly governed by State rent-control law (checked by the words 'rent control'). Lawyer: confirm.

questions.question: I lent my friend money three years ago. Is it too late to file a case to get it back?
